title: Deprecate legacy SAML2 adapters and mitigate OpenSSL compatibility issues
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Background: We still run two legacy SAML2 adapter implementations (python-saml-adapter-v1 and saml-bridge-legacy) in our auth gateway. Upgrading the platform OpenSSL stack (1.1.1 -> 3.x) surfaced compatibility failures in the adapters' native extensions and highlighted unsafe usage patterns in our JWT/OAuth token validation path. This ticket covers deprecating the legacy adapters, implementing compatibility shims for short-term stability, upgrading dependent JWT/OAuth libraries, and adding mitigations for OpenSSL-related edge cases.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Legacy adapters are marked deprecated in config and replaced by the consolidated 'sso-adapter-v2' in all internal customers' routes. 2) All services compiling native crypto extensions pass CI against OpenSSL 3.x and 1.1.1 in the matrix. 3) No high-severity Snyk/GHSA alerts remain for JWT/OAuth and SAML deps. 4) Unit and integration tests cover fallback shim behavior and verify cached JWT verifications. 5) Rollout plan executed with canary showing zero auth failures for 48h before broad rollout.
rollout_plan: Phase A - Canary: enable 'sso-adapter-v2' for 5% of traffic in eu-west for 48h with feature flag. Monitor auth success rate, latency, and error budget. Phase B - Compatibility shim: Deploy shim that translates legacy assertion formats and polyfills older cipher selection for OpenSSL 3.x; enable shim behind feature flag. Phase C - Migrate: Gradually move remaining routes off legacy adapters over two cycles, then flip deprecation flag to serve 100% with new adapter. Phase D - Cleanup: Remove shim and legacy code paths after 2 weeks stable and after security sign-off.
test_plan: - Create CI matrix jobs for python 3.10/3.11 with OpenSSL 1.1.1 and 3.1. - Add fuzz tests for SAML assertion parsing and JWT header edge cases. - Add integration smoke tests exercising SSO flow end-to-end with signed assertions. - Performance test: compare token validation latency before/after caching on a representative workload (auth benchmarking dashboard).
implementation_notes: - Introduce per-issuer JWT verification cache with TTL tied to jwks_cache_ttl to avoid repeated signature verification on bursty flows. - Refactor validator to use cryptography.io high-level API rather than custom OpenSSL bindings where possible. - Keep a thin compatibility shim that patches legacy PEM header parsing and supplies a restricted cipher list when OpenSSL 3.x rejects legacy defaults. - Avoid long-lived global OpenSSL init calls that block worker threads; move init into async-once startup path. - Coordinate with infra to provide images for both OpenSSL 1.1.1 and 3.x for canaries.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: incompatibility causes auth failures for partners still using older SAML metadata. Mitigation: keep shim enabled for 2 weeks of canary traffic and provide partner migration guidance. Risk: introducing JWT cache could hide key rotation; mitigation: cache keyed by (issuer,kid) and honor short cache TTLs plus cache-bust on 401s.
